meta.title: OS-15500 — How a Card Refund Paid Out Without Debiting Float

views.label: The float gate
views.note: The empty-string MerchantIdentifier satisfies the null check and the deduction is skipped.

views.label: Money leaves anyway
views.note: The payout proceeds and the API answers 200 with no error.

messages.label: MerchantIdentifier = ""
messages.note: Empty string, not NULL — upstream card feed changed on 2026-08-04

messages.label: UpdateFloatBalance() never reached
messages.note: skipFloatChecks = (cardTransaction?.MerchantIdentifier != null) is true for "" — RefundService.cs:1622

cards.title: The defect
items: An empty string is not null, so the guard treats it as a valid merchant identifier
The float deduction is skipped and the refund still pays out real money
FloatService is never entered — its lifeline stays inactive for the whole request

cards.title: Why nothing alerted
items: The API returns HTTP 200 with status ok and error null
APM records the trace as healthy, so no error or latency signal exists
The single skip log line is info-level and had no monitor attached

cards.title: Fixed 2026-09-04
items: Guard changed to !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(...) in commit e391ed8b
First correctly debited card refund after deploy: 2026-09-04 11:19:25 UTC
A real merchant identifier still skips float, which remains intended behaviour
